catalog_quote: [p.357] Since e and o only occur in stressed syllables, they alternate with i and u, which are present in their stead in unstressed positions, e.g. ƾănu ‘boat’ : poss. 1sg ƾănoj° : 3sg ƾănuta ... with stress regularly on non-final odd and pre-schwa syllables. ... [p.359] One of the salient features of the schwa is that it makes the preceding syllable stressed, which explains why the mid vowels e o can occur in positions such as dat.sg /vƝd'akǀn/ = wejaqkon° of /vƝd'aku/ = wejaqku ‘dog’ (Sammallahti 1974: 47), and Sammallahti’s comment that “closed final syllables receive secondary stress as a rule” (29) refers exactly to this state of affairs ... the imperfective participle of pan°tyosy° ‘to be full’ is pan°tyota because tyo is the third syllable of a tetrasyllabic word and therefore stressed ... [p.367] The stress placement in Proto-Nenets was straight-forward, with every non-final odd…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every fragment of the deciding quotation is present verbatim in the Salminen 2007 PDF we hold/text at pp.350, 357, 359 and 367 as cited. (2) Deciding source: a 2007 phonology article by the field's leading specialist; stress is stated as a by-product of the vowel-alternation analysis rather than in a dedicated section, but the rule (non-final odd syllables + pre-schwa syllables; schwa syllables unstressed) is explicit and is independently restated and endorsed by two held later sources (Burkova/IJaz RAN minlang page; Agicheva, Kozlov & Toldova 2026 fieldwork: 'confirms the validity of Salminen's system'). (3) New evidence downloaded now: Normanskaja 2025, the only instrumental study of Forest Nenets prominence, concludes there is no contrastive ('смыслоразличительное') stress, with intensity maxima mostly on the first syllable and duration maxima often on an open second syllab

sources.note: Current reference chapter covering Forest Nenets; per Normanskaja 2025:185 it states stress 'usually on the first syllable or on a non-first closed syllable' - a closed-syllable (weight) formulation that differs in wording from Salminen's odd/pre-schwa rule and from Burkova's own minlang page (held: 'first or non-first odd syllable'); worth reading verbatim to settle the weight hedge.

sources.note: The primary field phonology on which Salminen 2007 builds; our record quotes its stress statement only second-hand (Salminen p.359 quoting p.29). Normanskaja 2025:185 paraphrases pp.29-31 as containing a vowel-quantity clause (stress shifts to a long 2nd syllable after a short 1st) that bears directly on the 'weight-hedged'/what counts as heavy: coding and is not addressed in our quote.
